correctness.rationale: For odd m>=5 and theta=(m-1)/(4m), choose s as the integer nearest m/4. Every arbitrary correspondence of smaller-than-2pi theta distortion permits a selection f from m indices to four labels with each step-s pair forced to have target distance 1/4 (rather than 0 or 1/2). Hence f alternates parity along every orbit of addition by s. Each orbit has odd length m/gcd(m,s), contradiction. For the explicit surjection with four consecutive block sizes (k+1,k,k,k) if m=4k+1 and (k+1,k+1,k+1,k) if m=4k+3, pairwise discrepancy is <=theta in circumference-normalized units for same, adjacent and opposite target labels. Thus all-correspondence lower and constructive upper bounds match. Rebuilt exact arithmetic checker succeeded for 199 odd sizes, including 48,780 small surjective maps; finite checks do not prove all-m quantifiers. Source: RESULT.md proof and check_odd_polygon.py.

originality.rationale: The new all-odd square-to-polygon exact Gromov–Hausdorff formula is not implied by inspected same-object sources. Lim–Mémoli–Smith explicitly pose all-pairs determination but prove circle-versus-sample and consecutive-cardinality cases; Talipov covers divisible and 2-/3-point cases; the closest published square-to-polygon result treats only m=4k+2 and explicitly leaves odd m outside its scope. The circle-geodesic metric and correspondence quantifiers were matched at the statement level. Unindexed equivalent priority is unresolved and disclosed.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural infinite missing subfamily of the explicitly stated exact regular-polygon Gromov–Hausdorff distance question, for the first source size beyond the equilateral-simplex cases. Combined with published divisible and even-nondivisible results, it closes the entire square-to-regular-sample profile. The odd-cycle bipartiteness obstruction is structural and handles arbitrary correspondences, and the complementary cyclic-block map proves sharpness. It is more than a finite table or a routine case substitution; the source paper posed the general question and existing special-case arguments leave odd m>=7 uncovered. Scope and historical priority risk are explicit.
